### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via listDrafts (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation; a method of class SysMetadataRepository))_
- `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`  _(via /packages/:id/commits (route, the route ledger binds it to client method packages.listCommits))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/meta/_drafts (route, the route ledger binds it to client method meta.listDrafts))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `333e75620cfac37a8de0f7de0c12c1c6b87eb92f` — the merge of head `2f2c6feea3975d5d90e448c2427ba5c19f8117db` into base `55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 333e75620cfac37a8de0f7de0c12c1c6b87eb92f && git checkout 333e75620cfac37a8de0f7de0c12c1c6b87eb92f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583 2f2c6feea3975d5d90e448c2427ba5c19f8117db && git checkout -B drift-repro 55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583 && git merge --no-ff 2f2c6feea3975d5d90e448c2427ba5c19f8117db

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Check Changeset is red here by design: DELIBERATE CORRECTION** · `domain:spec` seat 2 · session `session_01GZSPSQ5ArPjSJdxxuqwGoZ` · 2026-10-12T21:40Z · head `fe50ab688`

- **Gate:** `Check Changeset` (`.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`), at the step `node scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs --base "$MERGE_BASE"`. It runs on `pull_request` only, never on `merge_group`, and it is not a required context.
- **Cause:** this PR changes `.changeset/22877-member-selector.md`, which another PR added. That note has not been released yet. This is not a filename collision: this card's own note is `.changeset/23073-list-member.md`, a new file.
- **What changed under the note:** its line 49 said "The protocol's draft list (`GET /meta/_drafts`) does not include it." This PR makes `listDrafts` and `listCommits` serve `member`, so that sentence would ship false. Exactly that one sentence is rewritten: "The protocol's draft list (`GET /meta/_drafts`) and a package's commit timeline serve it too, on every entry of a template, with the canonical `en-US` spelled out." No other line of that file moves.
- **Not done, on purpose:** the old sentence is not restored from the base, and no `skip-changeset` label is applied (ruling D on #18375).
- **Confirmation:** a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record on this same head will name the edited note and judge the rewritten sentence. A PASS there is the written confirmation, and the red stays.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fe50ab6889502d229b5e0c48948535548ff8f909`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23073 (body and its 5 comments: triage 6129686435, claim 6131409879, dev report 6132899471, seat ACCEPT 6132937336, patch round 6133092518), the ruling they cite on #22877 (6116165299) and the stage-2 records 6128093700 / 6128724141; PR #23099 (body, its 2 comments, the 13-file list, the net diff `6662e3f59..fe50ab688` against `main`, +215/-20); the check-runs on `fe50ab688`, polled in this act at 2026-10-12T21:51Z. Nothing was built, run or re-run; every file was read at the head with `git show`.

**Check-runs on the head: 40. 30 `success`; 5 `skipped` (Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, the Dogfood matrix shard, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke); 1 `failure` (`Check Changeset`); 4 `in_progress` at the poll (Test Core 2/6, 3/6, 5/6, 6/6). Every lint, type-check, build, docs, size, claim, single-writer and governed-queue gate is green.** `Check Changeset` is red at step 12 alone ("Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR", the `check-empty-changeset.mjs --base` step), with one annotation naming `.changeset/22877-member-selector.md`: the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class the script itself names (`FOREIGN_CORRECTION_REMEDY`: do NOT restore it; say so on the PR and get it confirmed). Steps 13 (ADR-0087 disposition) and 15 (no-major guard) of the same job ran after it and are green, so the red withholds no other verdict. `pr-automation.yml` triggers on `pull_request` only, never `merge_group`, and `main`'s branch rules (`GET /rules/branches/main`) require Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core and TypeScript Type Check, not Check Changeset. The spec artifact gates (`check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs`) are steps of `Type Check · source gates`, green. The running shards do not carry this record's verdict; a red one re-judges the head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ListDraftsResponseSchema.drafts[].member` — right.** `z.string().optional()`, no strictness change, and the describe matches the serving (3 below): the discriminator value, the canonical member spelled out, present on every entry of a discriminated type, absent for a name-only type, the by-name doors' selector. Pinned in `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts` (the parse keeps `en-US` / `zh-CN`; the name-only entry has no `member` property).
2. **`ListPackageCommitsResponseSchema.commits[].items[].member` — right.** Same shape and describe, naming the right source: the stored revert plan's member, the one `revertCommit` acts on (`parseCommitItems` feeds both doors). Pinned in `package-lifecycle.test.ts`.
3. **`listDrafts` serving — right.** The repository header carries `member` only for a non-canonical member: `storedRowMemberHeader` spreads `overlayMemberValue`, which answers `null` for a NULL, blank or canonical column and `undefined` for a type with no discriminator, so `{}` in both cases. The protocol folds it through `bundleMemberDiscriminator(header.type, stored)`: for `email_template` the stored value, or `disc.canonical` (`en-US`) when absent; for every other type `undefined`, and the door then returns `header` itself, so a name-only entry has no `member` key at all, not an `undefined`-valued one. Pinned in `sys-metadata-repository-14938-list-drafts-updated-at.test.ts` (both bodies say `en-US`; the served member follows the column; the `object` draft's keys are exactly the six declared).
4. **`listCommits` serving — right.** The same fold over the plan item's `member` (absent for the canonical member and for name-only types, per `CommitPlanItem`); `item` is returned untouched when the fold answers `undefined`. Pinned in `protocol-14038-list-commits-created-at-iso.test.ts` (`en-US`, `zh-CN`, and no key on the `object` item).
5. **The served value is exactly what `?member=` takes back — right, by code, both ways.** Served `zh-CN`: `resolveBundleMemberSelector` returns the trimmed string, `memberOption` passes it, and the repository `where` sets `bundle_member = 'zh-CN'`. Served `en-US`: the selector returns `en-US`, `bundleMemberDiscriminator` answers the canonical member (the same `wantedMember` as no selector at all), and the repository maps the canonical value to `null`, so `bundle_member IS NULL` (`overlayMemberValue`; `packageScopedRowWhere`: "string → eq; null → IS NULL"), the very row the list spelled out as `en-US`. The REST GET's closed set carries `state` and `member` together (stage 2), so the changeset's `?state=draft&member=zh-CN` example is a legal request. Pinned end to end in the objectql harness: each listed member read back through `getMetaItem` answers its own wording, for the two drafts and for the commit's two items.
6. **One discriminated-type predicate — right.** Both doors reuse stage 2's `bundleMemberDiscriminator`, keyed on `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` (`email_template` only); no second type list, and nothing is read off the body.
7. **Public surface of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — right; `minor` covers it.** `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.listDrafts`'s return literal and `listCommits`'s `items` literal each gain `member?: string`; `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts` changes a docblock only, no shape.
8. **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec` — right.** `ListDraftsResponse` and `ListPackageCommitsResponse` widen by one optional key; no export is added, so `api-surface/api.json` (export names) rightly does not move. The regenerated `protocol.mdx` (one nested row) and `package-lifecycle.mdx` (the `items` cell; the generator renders one nesting level) are in sync by the green `check:docs` step.
9. **`@objectstack/client` — described truthfully.** `meta.listDrafts` returns `Promise of ListDraftsResponse` and `packages.listCommits` `Promise of ListPackageCommitsResponse`, both imported from `@objectstack/spec/api` and pinned `toEqualTypeOf` in `return-type-precision.test.ts`. The client ships no changed byte, so the changeset rightly carries no client line, and its sentence (the types the client returns gain the field) is exact. The client sits in the same `fixed` release group as spec, so a consumer's `@objectstack/client` bumps with it in any case.
10. **REST and runtime doors — right, pass-throughs.** `GET /meta/_drafts` answers `res.json(result)`; the dispatcher answers `success(data)` and `success({ commits })`; no re-projection and no response-schema parse strips the key. The CLI reads neither list.
11. **Comment-only docblocks (`CommitPlanItem`; the repository's `member` header) — right.** Both sentences this head makes false are rewritten; they lie outside the two serving regions and the dev flagged them.
12. **The inverted stage-2 pin in the objectql harness — right.** The old assertion (a commit item has no `member` key) was the opposite contract; keeping it would have failed the serving this card orders. The drafts-empty-after-discard assertion is kept.
13. **Hand-written docs — nothing owed.** No page under `content/docs` outside the generated reference states that either list lacks `member`; the Docs Drift rows name the two symbols for their authorization gates. The sibling objectui at the pinned `.objectui-sha` cannot break on an added optional key (Console Pin Gate skipped by filter, rightly); Studio's half is objectui#12271.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23073-list-member.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`; the body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening: a new declared response key)`, matching the PR body and the claim. Right: both packages publish a widened shape (① 1, 2, 7); `objectql` changes a test file only, and `rest`, `runtime` and `client` change no byte, so no further line is owed. Nothing is removed or renamed, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed (Check Changeset step 13 green: no declared-breaking changeset); no `major` (step 15 green). No `skip-changeset`: the diff publishes. Each sentence of the body was read against the code: the two doors, the `en-US` spelling, the `?state=draft&member=zh-CN` example, "the language the stored revert plan records", the client sentence (① 9). All true.
- `Clause-②:` line, `yes (widening)` — right. Two response schemas gain a declared key; no door's accept set changes.
- **The edited pending note: `.changeset/22877-member-selector.md`** (stage 2, unreleased, added by PR #23070). The diff rewrites exactly one line, 49, and one sentence of it; every other line is byte-identical to the base.
  - Kept sentence (line 49, first): "The entries that `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts` returns have an optional `member`, present for a draft of a non-`en-US` language." Still true of this head: `storedRowMemberHeader` spreads `{}` for the canonical member (① 3).
  - Before: "The protocol's draft list (`GET /meta/_drafts`) does not include it." False of this head (① 3), so it could not stay.
  - After: "The protocol's draft list (`GET /meta/_drafts`) and a package's commit timeline serve it too, on every entry of a template, with the canonical `en-US` spelled out." True of this head, clause by clause: both doors serve `member` (① 3, 4); "on every entry of a template": `bundleMemberDiscriminator` answers a value for every `email_template` entry; "with the canonical `en-US` spelled out": `disc.canonical` is served where the column is NULL or the plan key absent. One precision for the record, not a defect: for the commit timeline, "it" is the plan item's stored member rather than the repository header's; the sentence claims what is served, not its source, and the discriminator value is the same.
  - Everything else in the note, read against this head: line 38, "The draft list and the commit timeline keep the fields they declare.", stays true (they serve exactly what they now declare); the frontmatter, the five routes' closed sets, the selector's refusals and the `SchemaRegistry` / `MetadataMutationEvent` paragraphs describe stage 2's code, which this head does not touch. Nothing else in the note is now false.
  - The correction is the right remedy. Both notes ship in one release, and the stage-2 note also lands in the `rest` and `objectql` CHANGELOGs that `23073-list-member.md` does not reach; restoring the base sentence would ship it false. The seat answered the dev's open question with A (6132937336), the dev executed it as the one-sentence edit (6133092518), and the seat's PR note 6133122274 names the gate and the cause. The `Check Changeset` red is confined to that step and that file (above), and this record is the written confirmation it asks for.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev's deviations (report 6132899471):
1. `packages/objectql/src/environment-overlay-email-locale-restart.test.ts` outside the claim's literal paths — answered: it is the serving's real-engine pin and held the opposite assertion; the claim's "with their tests" covers it (① 12).
2. Two comment-only docblocks outside the serving regions — answered, right (① 11).
3. The canonical member spelled out rather than omitted — answered, right: triage's direction (carry `member` for a discriminated type, nothing for a name-only type) is met by key presence, and the ruling's "NULL means the canonical member" is a storage rule the serving maps back exactly (① 3 to 5).
4. Two `origin/main` merges through `os-regen-merge.sh` — no regen deferral; the net diff against the merge base is the 13 files above and nothing from `main`.
5. Three stray files at the dev container's filesystem root (`/full1.pid`, `/gates2.err`, `/gates2.txt`) — not in the repo, not in the diff, nothing in this head. Escalated to the seat as container housekeeping, not a contract matter.
6. Zero label writes; no `skip-changeset` — right (②).

Open question (the stale stage-2 sentence; options A / B / C) — answered A by the seat, executed on this head, judged under ②.

Out-of-scope finding (the package-batch result arrays `published[]` / `failed[]`, `discarded[]` / `failed[]`, `reverted[]` / `failed[]` carrying `{ type, name }` only, so two members of one template read identically there too), carried in the PR's acceptance notes as noted, not filed — it is the same family as this card, read against declared response shapes (`PublishPackageDraftsResponseSchema`, `DiscardPackageDraftsResponseSchema`, `RevertPackageCommitResponseSchema`); not this PR's surface and no regression of this head. Escalated to the seat: file it as a card from that contract text, or record on the card why not. Prime Directive #10 leaves the filing the seat's; this record does not bury it.

The stage-2 records' carried escalations (the runtime dispatcher's item GET without `member`; `PUT`'s closed set) are not this PR's and are not reopened here.

- **The hop's commits:**
